root_cause.text: An integer type mismatch in nouveau_gem_pushbuf_reloc_apply() caused the pushbuf relocation bounds check to add a __u32 reloc_bo_offset and literal 4 in 32-bit arithmetic, allowing wraparound and bypass of the buffer object size validation.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit explicitly states that `r->reloc_bo_offset` is `__u32`, `4` is promoted to `unsigned int`, so `r->reloc_bo_offset + 4` "is performed in 32 bits and wraps before the comparison against the size_t bo size"; the patch fixes this by changing the check from `r->reloc_bo_offset + 4 > nvbo->bo.base.size` to `(u64)r->reloc_bo_offset + 4 > nvbo->bo.base.size`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix relocation bounds checking by promoting the offset to 64-bit before addition so oversized offsets cannot bypass the buffer size check.
intent_record.what: The bounds check in nouveau_gem_pushbuf_reloc_apply() was changed to cast r->reloc_bo_offset to u64 before adding 4 in the comparison against nvbo->bo.base.size: `r->reloc_bo_offset + 4 > nvbo->bo.base.size` became `(u64)r->reloc_bo_offset + 4 > nvbo->bo.base.size`.
intent_record.how: This makes the relocation offset arithmetic use 64-bit width during the size check, preventing incorrect overflow or truncation in the addition before comparing against the buffer object's size, so out-of-bounds relocations are detected reliably.

grouping_result.intent: Fix relocation bounds checking by promoting the offset to 64-bit before addition so oversized offsets cannot bypass the buffer size check.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly fixes the root cause: it addresses the integer type mismatch in relocation bounds checking by promoting the relocation offset to 64-bit before adding 4, preventing 32-bit wraparound from bypassing the buffer size validation.

candidates.rationale: This is the vulnerable bounds check expression. Because r->reloc_bo_offset is a __u32, adding 4 here is performed in 32-bit arithmetic, allowing wraparound before comparison against the buffer size.

vuln_statements.explanation: This pre-fix bounds check performs r->reloc_bo_offset + 4 using the 32-bit type of reloc_bo_offset, allowing integer wraparound before comparing against the buffer object size and thereby bypassing relocation bounds validation.

bic_trace_step.reason: The diff includes the full body of the relevant function `nouveau_gem_pushbuf_reloc_apply()`, so it is sufficient to judge the presence of the vulnerable bounds check. The vulnerable construct is present in the new check: `if (unlikely(r->reloc_bo_offset + 4 > nvbo->bo.mem.num_pages << PAGE_SHIFT)) { ... }`. Per the root cause, `r->reloc_bo_offset` is a `__u32`, and the literal `4` is also 32-bit, so `r->reloc_bo_offset + 4` is performed in 32-bit arithmetic and can wrap before comparison. That means a large offset near `UINT32_MAX` can bypass the intended bounds validation against the BO size. There is no cast or widening to a larger integer type in this expression, nor any alternative overflow-safe check such as comparing `r->reloc_bo_offset > size - 4`. Therefore the buggy check is present and the fix is not yet present.
